questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Total Change of a Function Given Its Rate of Change
questions.problem:
A pipe is filling water into a tank. The rate $r(t)$ at which water enters the tank is given by the function 

$$
r(t)=\frac{15}{1+7{t}^{2}},
$$

where $r(t)$ is measured in liters per minute, and $t>0$ is the time in minutes since the pipe started running. Initially, there were $60$ liters of water in the tank.

Which integral gives the quantity of water in the tank $t$ minutes after the inlet started running?
questions.worked_solution:
We're given the **rate of change** of volume $r(t).$ To find the total volume $V(t)$ after $t$ minutes, we apply the second fundamental theorem of calculus:

$$
\begin{aligned}V(t) & =V(0)+{\int }_{0}^{t}\frac{15}{1+7{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =60+{\int }_{0}^{t}\frac{15}{1+7{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

To ensure that our final function is a function of $t$ only, we use a different variable ($x$) for the integration.

questions.problem:
The rate at which guests check into a particular hotel one evening is given by the function

$$
r(t)=3{t}^{2}+2,
$$

where $r(t)$ is measured in guests per hour and $t>0$ is the time in hours since $\text{6}\,\text{p.m}.$

Guests are also checking out of the hotel at a steady rate of $1$ guest per hour.

If there were $200$ guests in the hotel at $6\,\text{p.m},$ how many guests will there be in the hotel at $9\,\text{p.m?}$
questions.worked_solution:
Guests are entering the hotel at a rate of $3{t}^{2}+2$ guests per hour and are leaving at a rate of $1$ guest per hour. Therefore, the **rate of change** in the number of guests (call it $R(t)$) is:

$$
\begin{aligned}R(t) & =r(t)-1 \\  & =3{t}^{2}+2-1 \\  & =3{t}^{2}+1\end{aligned}
$$

To find the **total number of guests** after $t$ hours (call it $T(t)$), we apply the second fundamental theorem of calculus:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =T(0)+{\int }_{0}^{t}R(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =200+{\int }_{0}^{t}(3{x}^{2}+1)\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

To ensure that $T$ is a function of $t$ only, we use a different variable ($x$) for the integration. 

To find out the number of guests after $3$ hours ($9\,\text{p.m}$), we substitute $t=3$ into the above, and evaluate.

$$
\begin{aligned}T(3) & =200+{\int }_{0}^{3}(3{x}^{2}+1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =200+{[{x}^{3}+x]|}_{0}^{3} \\  & =200+[(27+3)-(0)] \\  & =200+30 \\  & =230\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Global Minimum or Maximum of a Function Given Its Rate of Change
questions.problem:
The total number of participants $S(t)$ registered for an online conference after $t$ days is given by the function

$$
S(t)=40+{\int }_{0}^{t}(4x-16)\,\text{d}x,
$$

where $t>0$ is the time, in days, since the conference was announced. 

At what time is the number of participants at a minimum, and how many participants are registered at this time?
questions.worked_solution:
To find when the number participants is minimized, we need to solve $\frac{\text{d}S}{\text{d}t}=0.$ First, we differentiate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}S}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(40+{\int }_{0}^{t}(4x-16)\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(40)+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({\int }_{0}^{t}(4x-16)\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}{\int }_{0}^{t}(4x-16)\,\text{d}x \\  & =4t-16\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve $\frac{\text{d}S}{\text{d}t}=0$:

$$
4x-16=0\,⟹\,t=4
$$

So there are two candidates for global extrema, $t=0$ and $t=4.$ To find out how many participants are registered when $t=4,$ we figure out $S(4)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}S(4) & =40+{\int }_{0}^{4}(4x-16)\,\text{d}x \\  & =40+{[2{x}^{2}-16x]|}_{0}^{4} \\  & =40+[(2(4)^{2}-16(4))-(0)] \\  & =40-32 \\  & =8\end{aligned}
$$

Since $8<40$, we conclude that the minimum number of participants is $8$, and this occurs after $4$ days.

The minimum is $8$ participants  after $4$ days
The minimum is $40$ participants  after $0$ days
The minimum is $32$ participants  after $0$ days
The minimum is $40$ participants  after $4$ days

answer_fields.correct_value: The minimum is $8$ participants  after $4$ days

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Global Minimum or Maximum of a Function Given Its Rate of Change
questions.problem:
Scientists are observing a colony of bugs. The population $P(t)$ of the colony is given by the function

$$
P(t)=27+{\int }_{0}^{t}(3{x}^{2}-12)\,\text{d}x,
$$

where $P$ is the number of bugs, and $t>0$ is the time (in days) since the observation started. 

At what time is the population of the colony a minimum, and what is the number of bugs at this time?
questions.worked_solution:
To find when the population is a minimum, we need to solve $\frac{\text{d}P}{\text{d}t}=0.$ First, we differentiate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}P}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(27+{\int }_{0}^{t}(3{x}^{2}-12)\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(27)+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({\int }_{0}^{t}(3{x}^{2}-12)\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}{\int }_{0}^{t}(3{x}^{2}-12)\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{t}^{2}-12\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve $\frac{\text{d}P}{\text{d}t}=0$ for $t>0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3{t}^{2}-12 & =0 \\ 3({t}^{2}-4) & =0 \\ {t}^{2} & =4 \\ t & =2\end{aligned}
$$

So there are two candidates for global extrema, $t=0$ and $t=2.$
To find the number of bugs when $t=2,$ we figure out $P(2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}P(2) & =27+{\int }_{0}^{2}(3{x}^{2}-12)\,\text{d}x \\  & =27+[{x}^{3}-12x]{|}_{0}^{2} \\  & =27+[(8-24)-(0)] \\  & =27-16 \\  & =11\end{aligned}
$$

Since $11<27$, we conclude that the minimum population is $11$ bugs, and this happens after $2$ days.

The minimum is $8$ bugs after $4$ days

questions.problem:
The value $P(t)$ of a painting is given by the function

$$
P(t)=250+{\int }_{0}^{t}({3}^{x/4}-27)\,\text{d}x,
$$

where $P$ is measured in dollars, and $t>0$ is the time (in years) since the painting was created. 

At what time is the value a minimum, and how much does the painting cost at this time, rounded to the nearest dollar?

The minimum value is
$$$
{{field-1}}
after
{{field-2}}
years.
questions.worked_solution:
To find when the value is minimized, we need to solve $\frac{\text{d}P}{\text{d}t}=0.$ First, we differentiate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}P}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(250+{\int }_{0}^{t}({3}^{x/4}-27)\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(250)+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({\int }_{0}^{t}({3}^{x/4}-27)\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}{\int }_{0}^{t}({3}^{x/4}-27)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={3}^{t/4}-27\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve $\frac{\text{d}P}{\text{d}t}=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{3}^{t/4}-27 & =0 \\ {3}^{t/4} & ={3}^{3} \\ \frac{t}{4} & =3 \\ t & =12\end{aligned}
$$

So there are two candidates for global extrema, $t=0$ and $t=12.$ To find out the value of the painting when $t=12,$ we figure out $P(12):$

$$
\begin{aligned}P(12) & =250+{\int }_{0}^{12}({3}^{x/4}-27)\,\text{d}x \\  & =250+{[\frac{4\cdot {3}^{x/4}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}-27x]|}_{0}^{12} \\  & =250+[(\frac{4\cdot 27}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}-324)-(\frac{4\cdot 1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3})] \\  & =250-324+\frac{108-4}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\  & =-74+\frac{104}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\  & ≈21,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to the nearest integer.

Since $21<250,$ we conclude that the minimum value is $$\,21$, and this happens after $12$ years.
